@language.description: The Settings page's field label for the language the app shows.

@languageSystem.description: The Language row's first choice: the app shows the language the system prefers.

@trayOpen.description: The tray menu's item that shows the main window.

@loginTitle.description: The login window's title, and the signed-out account card's button that opens it.

loginSubtitle: Signing in connects to the Bitwarden identity server; Windows Hello must confirm before the key is written to this machine's credential manager.

@loginSubtitle.description: The login window's line under the title, saying what signing in does.

@loginEmail.description: The login form's label for the account email field.

@loginEmailPlaceholder.description: The login form's placeholder in the email field.

@loginPassword.description: The login form's label for the master password field.

@loginPasswordPlaceholder.description: The login form's placeholder in the master password field.

@loginAdvanced.description: The login form's disclosure that hides the server address field.

@loginServer.description: The login form's label for the server address field, shown under Advanced.

loginServerHint: The official Bitwarden cloud is the default. For self-hosting, enter your own address, for example https://vault.example.com; it is normalized by the official rules on submit.

@loginServerHint.description: The login form's hint under the server address field.

@loginSubmit.description: The login form's primary button that starts the password login.

@loginCancel.description: The login window's button that abandons the attempt.

loginReLogin: Sign in again (to refresh the key)

@loginReLogin.description: The configured account card's button that opens the login window to refresh the stored key.

@loginSpinnerLoggingIn.description: The login form's spinner label while the password login runs.

@loginBusySigningIn.description: The text next to the login form's spinner, and the status line while the password login runs.

@loginTwoFactorMethod.description: The label of the segmented control that picks among offered two-factor methods.

loginTwoFactorPrompt: The server asks for two-factor authentication: {method}

@loginTwoFactorPrompt.description: The hint above the code field, naming the selected second factor.

@loginCode.description: The generic label of the two-factor code field.

@loginCodeEmail.description: The two-factor code field's label when the code is emailed.

@loginCodeYubiKey.description: The two-factor code field's label for the YubiKey method.

loginCodeHint: The 6-digit code from the authenticator app

@loginCodeHint.description: The two-factor code field's placeholder for code methods without a more specific hint.

@loginCodeHintEmail.description: The two-factor code field's placeholder when the code is emailed.

loginCodeHintYubiKey: The 44-character password the YubiKey shows after it is touched

@loginCodeHintYubiKey.description: The two-factor code field's placeholder for the YubiKey method.

@loginSendEmailCode.description: The login form's button that asks the server to email the two-factor code.

@loginEmailCodeSent.description: The confirmation next to the send-code button once the code went out.

loginEmailCodeSentTo: The code will be sent to {email}

@loginEmailCodeSentTo.description: The hint under the email code's send button, naming the address the code goes to.

@loginUnsupportedAlso.description: The hint naming the offered methods biowarden cannot answer, after the ones it can.

note.example: this method is not supported by biowarden yet

@loginUnsupportedOffered.description: The panel's line listing every method the server offered, when none can be answered.

loginUnsupportedTitle: This method is not supported by biowarden yet. Use the extraction script under Advanced on the account page to enter the key.

@loginUnsupportedTitle.description: The panel shown when the server offers only methods biowarden cannot answer.

loginUnsupportedNote: this method is not supported by biowarden yet, so use the extraction script under Advanced on the account page to enter the key

@loginUnsupportedNote.description: The same explanation as loginUnsupportedTitle, worded to follow the semicolon in loginUnsupportedAlso.

@loginSubmitCode.description: The login form's primary button that answers the two-factor challenge.

@loginSpinnerVerifying.description: The two-factor form's spinner label while the code is submitted.

@loginSpinnerCancelling.description: The unsupported-method panel's spinner label while the attempt is cancelled.

@loginMethodAuthenticator.description: The name of the authenticator-app second factor.

@loginMethodEmail.description: The name of the emailed-code second factor.

@loginMethodYubiKey.description: The name of the YubiKey second factor.

@loginMethodDuo.description: The name of the Duo second factor.

@loginMethodWebAuthn.description: The name of the WebAuthn second factor.

@loginMethodRecoveryCode.description: The name of the recovery-code second factor.

@loginMethodListSeparator.description: The separator between second-factor method names in a list: a comma in English, an enumeration comma in Chinese.

loginNoticeBadServer: The server address is invalid; fix it and try again.

@loginNoticeBadServer.description: The login window's status line when the server address was refused.

loginNoticeTwoFactor: The server asks for two-factor authentication; enter the code.

@loginNoticeTwoFactor.description: The login window's status line when the password step stopped for a second factor.

loginNoticeCodeRejected: The code was not accepted; check it and try again.

@loginNoticeCodeRejected.description: The login window's status line when the server rejected the two-factor code.

@loginNoticeVerifying.description: The login window's status line while a two-factor code is submitted.

@loginNoticeEmailSent.description: The login window's status line after the code email went out.

@loginNoticeEmailSentTo.description: The login window's status line after the code email went out, naming the address.

@loginNoticeLoggedIn.description: The account page's notice after a login succeeded.

@loginNoticeCancelled.description: The account page's notice after the login attempt was cancelled.

loginNoticeBusy: A login is in progress; wait or click Cancel.

@loginNoticeBusy.description: The login window's status line when it is closed while a call is in flight.

loginErrorBadCredentials: The email or master password is incorrect

@loginErrorBadCredentials.description: The login failure when the server rejected the password.

loginErrorForbidden: The server refused the login: the account may be locked or need extra verification

@loginErrorForbidden.description: The login failure when the server forbade the attempt.

loginErrorCaptcha: The server asks for a CAPTCHA; sign in once in the browser and try again

@loginErrorCaptcha.description: The login failure when the server demanded a CAPTCHA.

loginErrorNetwork: Cannot reach the server; check the network and the server address

@loginErrorNetwork.description: The login failure when the server could not be reached.

loginErrorServer: The server returned an error; try again later

@loginErrorServer.description: The login failure when the server answered with an error.

loginErrorNoTwoFactorMethod: The server asks for two-factor authentication but offered no usable method

@loginErrorNoTwoFactorMethod.description: The login failure when the server required a second factor but returned no methods.

loginErrorNoChallenge: There is no login waiting for a code; enter the email and master password first

@loginErrorNoChallenge.description: The two-factor submission failure when no challenge is parked.

@loginErrorEmptyCode.description: The two-factor submission failure when the code is empty.

@loginErrorServerAddress.description: The server-address refusal, with the validator's own explanation.

detail.example: auth: base URL "http://bad host" has no host

@loginErrorFlowState.description: The login failure when the flow stopped in a state the UI cannot use.

loginErrorFlowStart: The login flow started in an unexpected state: {state}

@loginErrorFlowStart.description: The login failure when the start step answered with an unexpected state.

@loginErrorSaveKey.description: The login failure when the credential store refused the key write.

loginErrorProviderNotOffered: The server did not offer this method (provider {provider})

@loginErrorProviderNotOffered.description: The two-factor submission failure when the provider was never offered.

loginErrorEmailMethodMissing: The server did not offer the email code method

@loginErrorEmailMethodMissing.description: The send-email failure when the pending challenge has no email method.

loginErrorSessionPersist: The login session could not be persisted; the next start needs a fresh sign-in: {detail}

@loginErrorSessionPersist.description: The non-fatal warning when the refresh token could not be stored.

@loginStateLoggedOut.description: The account page's label for the signed-out login state.

@loginStateLoggingIn.description: The account page's label for the in-progress login state.

@loginStateNeeds2FA.description: The account page's label for the login state parked on a second factor.

@loginStateLoggedIn.description: The account page's label for the signed-in login state.
